**Finding submitted: deviation (rule IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data).**

- **What the document does:** §2(d) is the only ownership provision and covers only TrueLink's rights in the Interface. Nothing affirms that we retain rights in Client Content, Client Intellectual Property or the borrower/loan data flowing through the Interface (Client Content ownership appears only in §13, on discontinuation of hosting). The results of the Support Services — the programming customization we pay for — are addressed only as confidential/Client Proprietary Information (§§10(b), 10(c)), which is not ownership or a licence.
- **Aggravating factor:** §8(d) grants TrueLink a worldwide right to "use, distribute, disseminate, license, resell, exploit" Credit Data. That is a licence rather than an assignment (so not walk-away territory), and it is a negotiated bargain limited by the Credit Data definition and the Non-Competition Agreement, so I left it intact and expressly preserved it in the redline.
- **Why not compliant at fallback:** the fallback requires at minimum a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to deliverables; here there is neither ownership nor any surviving licence to paid-for work product, and no data ownership anchor.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** a single inserted §2(e) confirming Client ownership of content, IP and data, assignment of Support Services results, TrueLink's retained Interface IP with a perpetual licence back for embedded TrueLink IP, and no joint ownership — with the fallback offered in the comment.
